word_for_word: तेषां मनोराज्यं कथयन्नरकप्राप्तिमाह -- इदमद्येति चतुर्भिः। प्राप्स्ये प्राप्स्यामि। मनोरथं मनसः प्रियम्। शेषं स्पष्टम्। एषां त्रयाणां श्लोकानामित्यज्ञानविमोहिताः सन्तो नरके पतन्तीति चतुर्थेनान्वयः।

Describing their castles in the air, He states their attainment of hell in four verses beginning ‘This today.’ ‘I shall obtain’ means ‘I will acquire’; ‘desire’ means what is pleasing to the mind. The rest is clear. The first three verses are connected with the fourth: thus, deluded by ignorance, they fall into hell.
किंच -- असाविति। सिद्धः कृतकृत्यः। स्पष्टमन्यत्।
Further, ‘successful’ means one who considers himself to have accomplished everything that must be done. The rest is clear.

किंच -- आढ्य इति। आढ्यो धनादिसंपन्नः अभिजनवान्कुलीनः। यक्ष्ये यागाद्यनुष्ठानेनापि दीक्षितान्तरेभ्यः सकाशान्महतीं प्रतिष्ठां प्राप्स्यामि। दास्यामि स्तावकेभ्यश्च। मोदिष्ये हर्षं प्राप्स्यामीत्येवमज्ञानेन विमोहिताः मिथ्याभिनिवेशं प्रापिताः।

Further, ‘wealthy’ means possessed of wealth and the like; ‘high-born’ means from a noble family. ‘I shall sacrifice’ means: by performing sacrifices and other rites I shall gain great prestige surpassing other initiated sacrificers. ‘I shall give’ means to my flatterers, and ‘I shall rejoice’ means I shall experience delight. In this way they are deluded by ignorance and brought into false fixation.

एवंभूता यत्प्राप्नुवन्ति तच्छृणु -- अनेकेति। अनेकेषु मनोरथेषु प्रवृत्तं चित्तमनेकचित्तं तेन विभ्रान्ताः विक्षिप्ताः मोहमयेन जालेन समावृताः? मत्स्या इव सूत्रमयेन जानेन यन्त्रिताः। एवं कामभोगेषु सक्ता अभिनिविष्टाः सन्तोऽशुचौ कश्मले नरके पतन्ति।

Hear what people of this kind attain. Their mind is engaged in many fantasies and is therefore manifold; through it they are bewildered and distracted, enveloped in a net made of delusion, restrained like fish in a net of cords. Thus attached and deeply fixed in sensual enjoyments, they fall into a foul and impure hell.

यक्ष्य इति च यस्तेषां मनोरथ उक्तः स केवलं दम्भाहंकारादिप्रधान एव नतु सात्त्विक इत्यभिप्रायेणाह -- आत्मसंभाविता इति द्वाभ्याम्। आत्मनैव संभाविताः पूज्यतां नीताः नतु साधुभिः कैश्चित्। अतएव स्तब्धा अनम्राः? धनेन यो मानो मदश्च ताभ्यामन्विताः सन्तो नाममात्रेण ये यज्ञास्ते नामयज्ञाः। यद्वादीक्षितः सोमयाजी इत्येवमादिना नाममात्रप्रसिद्धये ये यज्ञास्तैर्यजन्ते। कथम्। दम्भेन नतु श्रद्धया। अविधिपूर्वकं च यथा भवति तथा।

The fantasy expressed by ‘I shall sacrifice’ is dominated only by hypocrisy, egoism and the like, not sattva. Therefore He says in two verses beginning ‘self-honored.’ They are honored only by themselves and raised to importance by themselves, not by any good people. Hence they are stiff and unbending. Endowed with pride and intoxication caused by wealth, they perform sacrifices that are sacrifices only in name, or sacrifices intended merely to gain labels such as ‘initiated sacrificer’ or ‘Soma-sacrificer.’ How? With hypocrisy rather than faith and in a manner contrary to prescribed rule.

अविधिपूर्वकत्वमेव प्रपञ्चयति -- अहंकारमिति। अहंकारादिसंश्रिताः सन्त आत्मपरदेहेषु स्वदेहेषु परदेहेषु च चिदंशेन स्थितं मां प्रद्विषन्तो यजन्ते। दम्भयज्ञेषु श्रद्धाया अभावादात्मनो वृथैव पीडा भवति। तथा पश्वादीनामपि अविधिना हिंसायां चैतन्यद्रोहमात्रमेवावशिष्यत इति प्रद्विषन्त इत्युक्तम्। अभ्यसूयकाः सन्मार्गवर्तिनां गुणेषु दोषारोपकाः।

He elaborates their acting without proper rule. Taking refuge in egoism and the rest, they sacrifice while hating Me, who abide as the conscious principle in their own and others’ bodies. In hypocritical sacrifices, because faith is absent, they merely torment their own bodies in vain; and when animals and others are injured contrary to rule, nothing remains except hostility toward consciousness itself. Therefore they are said to hate Me. ‘Fault-finders’ are those who attribute defects to the virtues of people following the right path.

तेषां कदाचिदप्यासुरस्वभावप्रच्युतिर्न भवतीत्याह -- तानिति द्वाभ्याम्। तानहं मां द्विषतः क्रूरान्संसारेषु जन्ममृत्युमार्गेषु? तत्रापि आसुरीष्वेवातिक्रूरासु व्याघ्रादियोनिषु अजस्रमनवरतं क्षिपामि। तेषां पापकर्मणां तादृशं फलं ददामीत्यर्थः।

He says in two verses that such people never fall away from their demonic nature. Those cruel persons who hate Me I repeatedly cast into saṃsāra, the paths of birth and death, and specifically into exceedingly cruel demonic wombs such as those of tigers. The meaning is that I give them a fruit corresponding to their sinful actions.
किंच -- आसुरीमिति। ते च मामप्राप्यैवेत्येवकारेण मत्प्राप्तिशङ्का कुतस्तेषां। मत्प्राप्त्युपायं सन्मार्गमप्यप्राप्य ततोऽप्यधमां गतिं कृमिकीटादियोनिं यान्तीत्युक्तम्। शेषं स्पष्टम्।

Further, the restrictive particle in ‘without attaining Me’ excludes even the possibility of their attaining Me. Failing even to reach the good path that is the means to attaining Me, they go to a still lower destiny, births such as worms and insects. The rest is clear.

उक्तानामासुरदोषाणां मध्ये सकलदोषमूलभूतं दोषत्रयं सर्वथा वर्जनीयमित्याह -- त्रिविधमिति। कामः क्रोधो लोभश्चेतीदं त्रिविधं नरकस्य द्वारम्। अतएवात्मनो नाशनं नीचयोनिप्रापकम्। तस्मादेतत्त्रयं सर्वात्मना त्यजेत्।

Among the demonic faults described, He says that the three faults forming the root of all faults must be wholly abandoned. Desire, anger and greed are the three gates of hell; therefore they destroy the self in the sense of leading it to low births. Hence these three must be abandoned completely.
त्यागे च विशिष्टफलमाह -- एतैरिति। तमसो नरकस्य द्वारभूतैरेतैस्त्रिभिः कामादिभिर्विमुक्तो नरः आत्मनः श्रेयःसाधनं तपोयोगादि कर्माचरति ततश्च मोक्षं प्राप्नोति।

He states the special fruit of abandoning them. A person freed from these three—desire and the rest, which are gates to the darkness of hell—performs practices conducive to his highest good, such as austerity and yoga, and thereby attains liberation.

कामादित्यागश्च स्वधर्माचरणं विना न भवतीत्याह -- य इति। शास्त्रविधिं वेदविहितं धर्ममुत्सृज्य यः कामकारतो यथेच्छं वर्तते स सिद्धिं तत्त्वज्ञानं न प्राप्नोति। नच सुखमुपशमं नच परां गतिं मुक्तिं प्राप्नोति।

Abandonment of desire and the rest is impossible without performing one’s own dharma. Therefore He says: whoever rejects scriptural rule, the dharma enjoined by the Veda, and acts arbitrarily under the impulse of desire attains neither perfection, meaning knowledge of reality, nor happiness and tranquility, nor the supreme goal, liberation.

फलितमाह -- तस्मादिति। इदं कार्यमिदमकार्यमित्यस्यां व्यवस्थायां ते तव शास्त्रं श्रुतिस्मृतिपुराणादिकमेव प्रमाणम्। अतः शास्त्रविधानोक्तं कर्म ज्ञात्वा इह कर्माधिकारे वर्तमानो यथाऽधिकारं कर्म कर्तुमर्हसि। तन्मूलत्वात्सत्त्वशुद्धिसम्यग्ज्ञानमुक्तीनामित्यर्थः।

He states the conclusion. In determining ‘this should be done’ and ‘this should not be done,’ scripture—Śruti, Smṛti, Purāṇa and the rest—is your valid authority. Therefore, knowing the action taught by scriptural injunction and while situated here where action is to be performed, you should act according to your eligibility, because purity of mind, right knowledge and liberation all have that as their basis.
